## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Abhirūpanandātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.1) is a poem belonging to the *Therīgāthā* in the Khuddaka Nikāya. It consists of verses 19 and 20 of the collection, which according to Dhammapāla's commentary (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*) were addressed by the Buddha directly to the nun Abhirūpanandā [Collett 2014]. In the commentarial account, Abhirūpanandā, excessively attached to and proud of her personal beauty, initially avoided an audience with the Buddha; upon finally appearing before him, the Buddha conjured a vision of a beautiful woman and made it wither away in front of her, inducing spiritual urgency (*saṃvega*) before uttering these verses on the impermanence and foul nature of the body [Collett 2014].
